title: adaptive-health-probe-throttler-and-local-fallback-optimizer-hotfix
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Patch: introduce adaptive backoff for health probes to reduce flapping and tune local fallback jitter. No API changes. Rollout staged to regional control planes.
description:
Motivation: We observed multiple incidents where transient network noise caused aggressive health probes to mark nodes/regions unhealthy, triggering unnecessary regional failovers and KV drain cycles. This resulted in cascading cold-starts and elevated P95s for a subset of tenants. This hotfix implements an adaptive probe throttler and local fallback optimizer to reduce probe-induced flapping while preserving fast detection for genuine outages.

What this PR does (summary): Introduces an adaptive backoff algorithm for health probes that factors recent probe jitter and request error-rate to avoid over-sampling a noisy endpoint. Adds a local-fallback optimizer that: 1) applies a short, randomized cooldown (jittered warm window) before initiating regional failover; 2) avoids KV drain when a node is temporarily flagged but passes a quick KV sync health check. Adds unit tests, small telemetry hooks, and a short operational runbook.

Key design decisions: - Backoff is per-probe-stream (service-region combination) and decays exponentially with a capped max interval. - We favor short local retries + KV quick-check over immediate region-level eviction to reduce the blast radius of transient flaps. - Jitter windows are deterministic per-lease-id to avoid correlated retries across nodes. - Telemetry emits probe_backoff_seconds and probe_suppressed_count so ops can monitor suppression behavior.

Commit summary: - feat(health): add adaptiveProbeScheduler and backoff state machine (probe_manager.go) - fix(failover): check kv_quick_sync before initiating full region eviction (decision_engine.go) - docs: operational guidance and rollout notes (docs/operational/health-probes.md) - test: deterministic unit tests for backoff decay and jitter logic (tests/health_backoff_test.go) - ci: add health simulation script for stress runs (scripts/ci/health-sim.sh)

Files changed (high level snippets): - services/health/probe_manager.go: added adaptiveProbeScheduler struct, new tick loop, and backoff decay logic. Example snippet: "if recentJitter > jitterThresh { backoff = min(backoff*2, maxBackoff) } else { backoff = max(minBackoff, backoff*0.9) }" - runtime/failover/decision_engine.go: added kvQuickSync check before scheduling eviction; changed EvictRegion(...) to EvictRegionIfKVUnsync(...) - configs/region/fallbacks.yaml: new defaults for probe_min_interval/probe_max_interval/probe_jitter_seed - telemetry/metrics.yaml: added probe_backoff_seconds gauge and probe_suppressed_count counter

Testing and validation: - Unit tests cover deterministic backoff trajectories and jitter seeding. - Local integration: ran health-sim.sh against a two-region dev cluster to reproduce previous noisy-probe pattern and verified suppressed flaps. - Staging: deployed to staging region for 24h with a controlled noise generator; observed 72% reduction in region-level evictions and no regression in true outage detection in injected-failure tests.

CI summary: - checks: go-lint (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-smoke (pass), e2e-staging (pass), build (pass). A flaky e2e was re-run once during author push; all checks passed on final commit.

Review conversation (high level timeline): - Mateo Silva (review): requested stronger documentation on the decay constants and suggested exposing probe_max_interval as an override in Dedicated. Author reply: added config override and included a note in configs/region/fallbacks.yaml. - Priya Kapoor (review): asked for a safety gate to ensure we never suppress probes permanently; suggested an upper bound. Author reply: added a hard cap (probe_max_interval) and a 'suppress_count_reset' window. - Noah Martinez (approval): validated tests, telemetry, and staging runs; approved with a single comment to include rollout notes in the release.

Operational rollout plan: - Phase 1: Canary rollout to 10% of control-plane traffic in us-west for 6h. Monitor probe_backoff_seconds, probe_suppressed_count, regional_eviction_count, and KV-drift alerts. - Phase 2: Expand to EU regions over 24h if metrics stable. - Phase 3: Global rollout with full telemetry retention and follow-up audit.

Rollback plan: - Toggle knob: configs/region/fallbacks.yaml contains probe_backoff_enabled flag; revert to false to return to legacy behavior immediately. - In case of unanticipated regression, we will revert the hotfix commit and redeploy within the hour.

Notes and follow-ups: - Follow-up ticket created (ENG-1983) to evaluate a machine-learned probe scheduler using historical latency/error-rate patterns. - Ops requested an alert when probe_suppressed_count spikes above 5% of total probes for more than 5 minutes (added to incident runbook).

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals. Post-merge, cherry-picked the fix into maintenance/release-2026-02 for an expedited private-customer patch.
